notebook.name: backlinks
notebook.title: List the pages linking to a page
notebook.description: List the pages that link to a page: each with its path, how many of its links lead there (1000 means 1000 or more) and the lines around the first ten of them, each at most 240 bytes. Only a page has backlinks: an attachment's path is not found. A page's links to itself are left out; a page written since the link index read it has no lines yet. Go on with next_cursor while it is set.

path.description: The page's path from the notebook's root, ending with .md.

limit.description: At most this many pages, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: batch
notebook.title: Apply several writes as one change
notebook.description: Apply up to 100 writes as one change, all or none, with a message the history shows. Each op is a write, edit, move or delete: op names the tool and its other members are that tool's arguments; it acts on the notebook as the ops before it left it, their paths and contents. base_version is a page's version from before the batch; a page the batch creates takes none. A refused op writes nothing at all: the error has its op, from 0, and that tool's code. A delete of a page whose descendants an earlier op deleted takes them in one deletion, the earlier op answering merged_into; a batch may not delete what it creates, renames or moves. Unlike separate calls, links follow the batch's renames and moves, merged node by node, from where they led before the batch, or, in a page the batch writes, at its latest write before them (on the tree then, with the aliases from before the batch): what other ops did in between to where they lead (creating, renaming, moving or deleting a page) is not seen, nor any alias the batch changed. A page the batch writes or deletes that is being edited in the web editor refuses at the first op that writes or deletes it, as page.locked; one that only the links' rewrite of its renames and moves reaches is checked after those, as linking.pages_locked at its first rename or move. The answer has the changeset's id and time and each op's result, as many as fit, results_count all of them: changeset reads the rest. What the batch writes reaches the search some seconds after it: building says it is on its way. Each op's changed is what its tool would answer at that step; the batch's tells whether it left a change. In an LLM Wiki, one move of an existing subtree from outside into the source area may carry at most 10,000 nodes, including its root, empty pages and attachments; above that it is page.source_too_large. Known invalid destination, cycle, title, protection and reserved-name errors come first; the bound precedes depth errors in descendants not yet read. Ordinary moves, moves within or out of sources, and moves of the source root or an ancestor that keep source membership are unchanged. Move smaller subtrees into sources separately. Writes to each page are merged into its final body before the write unit runs. Source duplicate checks at creation and source entry use those merged bytes, so a batch can differ from the same tools called separately or from their apparent intermediate bodies. A refusal keeps the entire batch unchanged.

ops.description: The writes, applied in their order as one change: 1 to 100.

op.description: The tool this op is: write, edit, move or delete. Its other members are that tool's arguments.

path.description: write, edit and delete: the path, from the notebook's root, as that tool takes it.

content.description: write: the page's whole content, as it will be stored.

base_version.description: write and edit: the page's version as read before the batch. None for a page the batch creates.

old_string.description: edit: the text to replace, byte for byte, which must occur exactly once unless replace_all is set.

new_string.description: edit: the text to put in its place.

replace_all.description: edit: replace every occurrence of old_string. Default false.

from.description: move: the path of the page or attachment that moves.

to.description: move: the full path it will have, never a page to move it into.

update_links.description: move: rewrite the links to what moves so that they follow it. Default true.

recursive.description: delete: delete a page with its children. Default false.

message.description: Why the batch is made, shown with its change in the history: 1 to 4,096 bytes.

notebook.name: changeset
notebook.title: Read a changeset
notebook.description: Read one of the notebook's changesets by the id log gives: its kind, client, author, times, message, counts, what it reverts and what reverted it, and whether it renames or moves nodes; then what it did to each node it changed, a page at a time by node id: where the node was before and after in the tree, the revision of the content it wrote, and the node's current path (null when it is in the trash). The changeset itself comes on the first page, without cursor; go on with next_cursor while it is set. A changeset of another notebook is not found here. History is read-only here: people revert changesets in the web.

id.description: The changeset's id, as log gives it.

limit.description: At most this many changes, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: delete
notebook.title: Delete a page or an attachment
notebook.description: Put a page or an attachment in the notebook's trash, by its path from the notebook's root: people restore it from the trash in the web. A page with pages or attachments under it needs recursive set to true, which puts them in the trash with it. Any of its pages being edited in the web editor, by you too, refuses the deletion, saying by whom; the locks cannot be taken over. The answer has how many pages and attachments went to the trash, itself counted, and the changeset's id and time.

path.description: The path of the page or attachment to delete, from the notebook's root.

recursive.description: Delete a page with its children, its pages and attachments. Default false: a page with children is refused.

notebook.name: edit
notebook.title: Edit a page
notebook.description: Replace old_string with new_string in a page's content on the server, byte for byte, as a find and replace: old_string must occur exactly once (occurrences that overlap count), unless replace_all is set, which replaces each, left to right. Copy old_string from what read gave, with enough of the text around it to be unique: quotes and spaces are matched as they are. On a page whose line breaks are all CRLF and an old_string without CR, old_string's bare LFs are matched as CRLF and new_string's are written as CRLF (a CR in new_string stays); with a CR in old_string, both are taken as given. Without base_version, the edit applies to the content as it is now, made once more if the page changed while it was made; with base_version, it is refused when the page changed since. A page being edited in the web editor, by you too, refuses the edit, saying by whom; the lock cannot be taken over. The answer has the page's version, how many times old_string was replaced, changed (false when the content stayed as it was), and the changeset's id and time.

path.description: The page's path from the notebook's root, as "A/B.md": its ancestors' titles, then its own title and ".md".

old_string.description: The text to replace, copied from what read gave, byte for byte: 1 byte to 1 MiB.

new_string.description: The text to put in its place, which differs from old_string.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence of old_string, left to right. Default false: old_string must occur exactly once.

base_version.description: The page's version, as read, list or write gave it: the edit is refused when the page changed since. Without it, the edit applies to the content as it is now.

notebook.name: grep
notebook.title: Find lines by a regular expression
notebook.description: Find the lines of the notebook's pages that a Go regular expression (RE2 syntax, as ripgrep's default) matches, page by page in path order. Each hit has the page's path, the line's number as read counts lines (read with that offset and limit 1 gives the line) and the line's text as stored, without its \r and, on the first line, its byte order mark; a line over 1000 bytes is cut around its first match, cut true; column, when the text does not start at the line's first byte, is the byte it starts at, as read's column. Contents include their frontmatter; titles are not searched (list's glob finds them), nor attachments. glob keeps the pages whose paths it matches, as list's; ignore_case matches without case, as (?i). The pattern is at most 1024 bytes, without a newline, each line matched alone; one too complex, as large repeats, is refused. A call checks a bounded amount: go on with next_cursor while it is set. incomplete says the call stopped at its bounds before it checked every page it had to, so no hit is then no proof of none. partial_lines are lines too long to match whole within a call: read them. building says pages queued in bulk (by a batch, an import, a background restore or revert, an upgrade) are not searched until the index catches up. A page moved or written between calls, with its subpages, may be skipped or checked again. For words and Chinese text, search ranks pages and gives excerpts.

pattern.description: The Go regular expression (RE2), at most 1024 bytes, matched against each line alone. It is read in NFC, as the lines are: write a combining mark as an escape, such as \x{301}, to keep it apart from the character before it.

glob.description: Only the pages whose paths match this glob, as list's: "Projects/**", "**/*.md". Default: every page.

ignore_case.description: Match without case, as (?i). Default false.

limit.description: At most this many lines with a hit, 1 to 500. Default 100.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: index
notebook.title: List the notebook's pages by type, tag or parent
notebook.description: List the notebook's pages as its link index holds them: each with its path; its frontmatter's type and summary, the first key of that name whatever its case, when its value is text; its tags, 20 at most; when its content last changed; how many other pages link to it (1000 means 1000 or more); and its parent page's path. type, summary and each tag are cut to 256 bytes, cut naming what was cut. type keeps the pages of exactly that type; tag those with that tag or one under it ("plan" takes "plan/q4"; a leading # is dropped); parent the child pages of that page, "/" those at the root. Omit a filter rather than give it empty: "" is refused. The pages with a type come first, by type, then the others. A page the index has not read yet, as one written before nervewiki reindex after an upgrade, is not listed. Go on with next_cursor while it is set.

type.description: Only the pages whose frontmatter's type is exactly this.

tag.description: Only the pages with this tag or one under it, with or without its leading #.

parent.description: Only the child pages of this page, by its path ending with .md; "/" for the root's.

limit.description: At most this many pages, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: list
notebook.title: List nodes
notebook.description: List the notebook's pages and attachments. With pattern empty or "/", the root's children; with "A/B/", the children of the page A/B.md; both in the tree's order. Any other pattern is a glob over the paths, in path order: * matches within a segment, ? one character, ** any number of segments as a segment of its own ("**/*.md" is every page, "A/**" everything under A). Matching ignores case. Each item has its path, its kind (page or attachment) and whether it has children; a page also its version, size and last change, an attachment its type and size. An answer holds at most limit items and about 48 KiB, and a costly glob over a large notebook stops after a bounded amount of matching, maybe with no items: whenever next_cursor is set, pass it back as cursor to go on. A path without wildcards that names nothing may come with a hint, as when it names a page without its .md.

pattern.description: "" or "/" for the root's children, "A/B/" for the children of A/B.md, or a glob. Default: the root's children.

limit.description: At most this many items, 1 to 1000. Default 200.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: log
notebook.title: List the notebook's changes
notebook.description: List the notebook's changesets, newest first: what people and agents changed, each with its kind, client, author (id and display name), times, message, how many nodes and contents it changed, what it reverts and what reverted it, and its first three changes; a changeset too large for the answer comes alone, its changes cut to fit and changes_cut true. path keeps the changesets that changed that page or attachment; actor those of an account, "me" for yours; client those of a client, "mcp" for every agent. A page or an attachment in the trash has no path: find its changesets in the whole log. Go on with next_cursor while it is set. changeset reads one in full. History is read-only here: people restore versions and revert changesets in the web.

path.description: Only the changesets that changed the page or attachment at this path, from the notebook's root.

actor.description: Only the changesets by this account: its id, or "me" for yours.

client.description: Only the changesets of this client: "web", "api", "cli", "mcp:<name>" for an agent, or "mcp" for every agent.

limit.description: At most this many changesets, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: move
notebook.title: Move or rename a page or an attachment
notebook.description: Move, rename, or both at once, a page or an attachment: from is its path, to the full path it will have, both from the notebook's root ("Archive/Plan 2026.md"), never a page to move it into. A page's path ends with .md, and an attachment's keeps an extension, which may change. A page moves with its children. The page above to must exist: move creates no pages. The links to what moves, and to its pages, are rewritten to follow it, unless update_links is false, which leaves every page linking to it as it is: those links may then lead elsewhere, or nowhere. Rewriting the links of a page being edited in the web editor, by you too, is refused, saying by whom; the lock cannot be taken over. The answer has the new path, node_id, changed, and the changeset's id and time (null when nothing moved). In an LLM Wiki, one move of an existing subtree from outside into the source area may carry at most 10,000 nodes, including its root, empty pages and attachments; above that it is page.source_too_large. Known invalid destination, cycle, title, protection and reserved-name errors come first; the bound precedes depth errors in descendants not yet read. Ordinary moves, moves within or out of sources, and moves of the source root or an ancestor that keep source membership are unchanged. Move smaller subtrees into sources separately.

from.description: The path of the page or attachment to move, from the notebook's root.

to.description: The full path it will have, its new name last: never a page to move it into. The page above it must exist.

update_links.description: Rewrite the links to what moves, and to its pages, so that they follow it. Default true.

notebook.name: read
notebook.title: Read a page or an attachment
notebook.description: Read a page or an attachment by its path from the notebook's root; a page's path ends with .md. A page comes as two text blocks: a line of JSON metadata (path, kind, version, offset, column, lines, total_lines, byte_size, next_offset, next_column), then its lines exactly as stored, frontmatter, byte order mark and CRLF included. offset is the first line, from 1; limit the number of lines, 2000 by default. An answer holds about 48 KiB at most, its metadata line included: go on from next_offset, and from next_column when a line was too long for one answer; the parts read in turn are the whole content. An attachment comes as its metadata (type, size, SHA-256, width and height, how to link it, a download address valid for an hour or two), then the image itself for a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP of at most 3 MiB and 8000 pixels a side, or else a link to download it. Without the server's public address set (server.public_url) there is no download address: an image still comes itself, any other attachment as its metadata only, with a note saying so.

path.description: The path from the notebook's root: "A/B.md" for a page, "A/diagram.png" for an attachment.

column.description: The byte of the first line to start from, from 0: next_column of the previous answer. Default 0.

limit.description: At most this many lines, from 1. Default 2000.

notebook.name: search
notebook.title: Search the notebook's words
notebook.description: Full-text search of the notebook for words: the pages and attachments whose titles hold every term come first, then the pages whose contents do, each newest first, a page with an excerpt around its first hit. Terms are parted by spaces and match without case; Chinese text matches by pairs of characters, so a term of one Chinese character finds titles only. q is at most 256 bytes and 8 terms. The first page has count: exact, about or at_least. A page may hold fewer results than limit, even none, and still a next_cursor: a call checks a bounded number of contents; go on while next_cursor is set. building says pages queued in bulk (by a batch, an import, a background restore or revert, an upgrade) are not searched until the index catches up. For patterns, exact text and line numbers, use grep.

q.description: The words to find, parted by spaces: at most 256 bytes and 8 words.

limit.description: At most this many results, 1 to 50. Default 20.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: versions
notebook.title: List or read a page's versions
notebook.description: Without revision, list a page's versions, newest first: each with its revision, size, times, and the changeset that wrote it (its kind, client and author); the answer also has the page's current version. Go on with next_cursor while it is set. With revision, read that version's content as read reads a page: two text blocks, a line of JSON metadata (path, kind, revision, current_version, offset, column, lines, total_lines, byte_size, next_offset, next_column), then its lines exactly as stored; go on from next_offset, and next_column. The version answered has its own revision, which may be above the one asked for: an edit session's saves share one version. Revisions are for reading: write and edit take the page's version, from read. A page in the trash has no path: its versions are read in the web.

path.description: The page's path from the notebook's root, as "A/B.md".

revision.description: The revision to read, from 1. Without it, the list of the page's versions.

offset.description: With revision: the first line, from 1. Default 1.

column.description: With revision: the byte of the first line to start from, from 0: next_column of the previous answer. Default 0.

limit.description: Without revision: at most this many versions, 1 to 100, default 50. With revision: at most this many lines, from 1, default 2000.

cursor.description: Without revision: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: write
notebook.title: Write a page
notebook.description: Write a page's whole content by its path from the notebook's root; the path ends with .md. Without base_version, it creates the page, and the parent pages it lacks, empty, in one change; a path that is a page already is refused. With base_version, the version read, list or write gave, it replaces the content of the page at the path: refused when the page changed since, or when the path names another page now; read it again. When the page holds that content already, nothing is written and changed is false, with an older base_version of that page too, and while the page is being edited. The content is stored byte for byte: at most 5 MiB of UTF-8, without NUL. A page being edited in the web editor, by you too, refuses the write, saying by whom; the lock cannot be taken over. The answer has the page's path, node_id and version, changed (false when nothing was written), the nodes it created, and the changeset's id and time.

path.description: The page's path from the notebook's root, as "A/B.md": its ancestors' titles, then its own title and ".md".

content.description: The page's whole content, as it will be stored: frontmatter, byte order mark and line breaks included.

base_version.description: The page's version, as read, list or write gave it, to replace its content. Without it, the page is created.

notebook.name: lint
notebook.title: Check the notebook's health
notebook.description: Check this notebook's health from a snapshot for this call. Omit rule for counts and previews of the applicable rules; limit and cursor require rule. Set rule to read its items, then continue with next_cursor; pages may move between calls. count_capped marks a lower bound, not the end of pagination. target_cut marks a shortened display target, not its full identity; use item_key. Page and source items include their full paths.

rule.description: An exact health check rule. Omit for counts and previews; limit and cursor require a rule.

limit.description: At most this many items, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to continue after its last item.

notebook.name: pending_sources
notebook.title: List undigested sources
notebook.description: List an LLM Wiki's undigested sources from a snapshot for this call. LLM Wiki only: a standard notebook is refused. This is the undigested_sources health check, with each source's path, kind, bytes and original created_at; empty source pages are omitted. Continue with next_cursor; pages may move between calls. Each item keeps its complete item_key and cursor.

limit.description: At most this many items, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to continue after its last item.

glob.description: Only the pages whose paths match this glob, as list's: "Projects/**", "**/*.md". Default: every page.

ignore_case.description: Match without case, as (?i). Default false.

limit.description: At most this many lines with a hit, 1 to 500. Default 100.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

account.name: index
account.title: List the notebook's pages by type, tag or parent
account.description: List the notebook's pages as its link index holds them: each with its path; its frontmatter's type and summary, the first key of that name whatever its case, when its value is text; its tags, 20 at most; when its content last changed; how many other pages link to it (1000 means 1000 or more); and its parent page's path. type, summary and each tag are cut to 256 bytes, cut naming what was cut. type keeps the pages of exactly that type; tag those with that tag or one under it ("plan" takes "plan/q4"; a leading # is dropped); parent the child pages of that page, "/" those at the root. Omit a filter rather than give it empty: "" is refused. The pages with a type come first, by type, then the others. A page the index has not read yet, as one written before nervewiki reindex after an upgrade, is not listed. Go on with next_cursor while it is set.

type.description: Only the pages whose frontmatter's type is exactly this.

tag.description: Only the pages with this tag or one under it, with or without its leading #.

parent.description: Only the child pages of this page, by its path ending with .md; "/" for the root's.

limit.description: At most this many pages, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

account.name: list
account.title: List nodes
account.description: List the notebook's pages and attachments. With pattern empty or "/", the root's children; with "A/B/", the children of the page A/B.md; both in the tree's order. Any other pattern is a glob over the paths, in path order: * matches within a segment, ? one character, ** any number of segments as a segment of its own ("**/*.md" is every page, "A/**" everything under A). Matching ignores case. Each item has its path, its kind (page or attachment) and whether it has children; a page also its version, size and last change, an attachment its type and size. An answer holds at most limit items and about 48 KiB, and a costly glob over a large notebook stops after a bounded amount of matching, maybe with no items: whenever next_cursor is set, pass it back as cursor to go on. A path without wildcards that names nothing may come with a hint, as when it names a page without its .md.

pattern.description: "" or "/" for the root's children, "A/B/" for the children of A/B.md, or a glob. Default: the root's children.

limit.description: At most this many items, 1 to 1000. Default 200.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

account.name: log
account.title: List the notebook's changes
account.description: List the notebook's changesets, newest first: what people and agents changed, each with its kind, client, author (id and display name), times, message, how many nodes and contents it changed, what it reverts and what reverted it, and its first three changes; a changeset too large for the answer comes alone, its changes cut to fit and changes_cut true. path keeps the changesets that changed that page or attachment; actor those of an account, "me" for yours; client those of a client, "mcp" for every agent. A page or an attachment in the trash has no path: find its changesets in the whole log. Go on with next_cursor while it is set. changeset reads one in full. History is read-only here: people restore versions and revert changesets in the web.

path.description: Only the changesets that changed the page or attachment at this path, from the notebook's root.

actor.description: Only the changesets by this account: its id, or "me" for yours.

client.description: Only the changesets of this client: "web", "api", "cli", "mcp:<name>" for an agent, or "mcp" for every agent.

limit.description: At most this many changesets, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

account.name: move
account.title: Move or rename a page or an attachment
account.description: Move, rename, or both at once, a page or an attachment: from is its path, to the full path it will have, both from the notebook's root ("Archive/Plan 2026.md"), never a page to move it into. A page's path ends with .md, and an attachment's keeps an extension, which may change. A page moves with its children. The page above to must exist: move creates no pages. The links to what moves, and to its pages, are rewritten to follow it, unless update_links is false, which leaves every page linking to it as it is: those links may then lead elsewhere, or nowhere. Rewriting the links of a page being edited in the web editor, by you too, is refused, saying by whom; the lock cannot be taken over. The answer has the new path, node_id, changed, and the changeset's id and time (null when nothing moved). In an LLM Wiki, one move of an existing subtree from outside into the source area may carry at most 10,000 nodes, including its root, empty pages and attachments; above that it is page.source_too_large. Known invalid destination, cycle, title, protection and reserved-name errors come first; the bound precedes depth errors in descendants not yet read. Ordinary moves, moves within or out of sources, and moves of the source root or an ancestor that keep source membership are unchanged. Move smaller subtrees into sources separately.

from.description: The path of the page or attachment to move, from the notebook's root.

to.description: The full path it will have, its new name last: never a page to move it into. The page above it must exist.

update_links.description: Rewrite the links to what moves, and to its pages, so that they follow it. Default true.

account.name: notebooks
account.title: List your notebooks
account.description: List the notebooks you can see in every workspace you belong to, each with its id, its name, its workspace's slug and name, your role (admin, editor or reader) and its mode (standard, or llm_wiki for an LLM Wiki), by workspace, then by name. Open one with open_notebook, then pass its id as notebook to the other tools. truncated is true when there were more than one answer holds.

account.name: open_notebook
account.title: Open a notebook
account.description: Open a notebook: its mode (standard, or llm_wiki for an LLM Wiki), its instructions for agents (its root page AGENTS without its frontmatter, or the server's built-in ones when it has none) and an overview: how many pages and attachments it holds, when it last changed (null when nothing was ever written in it), and the nodes at its root. Follow its instructions while you work in it, and pass its id as notebook to the other tools. truncated is true when the root's nodes were cut short.

account.name: read
account.title: Read a page or an attachment
account.description: Read a page or an attachment by its path from the notebook's root; a page's path ends with .md. A page comes as two text blocks: a line of JSON metadata (path, kind, version, offset, column, lines, total_lines, byte_size, next_offset, next_column), then its lines exactly as stored, frontmatter, byte order mark and CRLF included. offset is the first line, from 1; limit the number of lines, 2000 by default. An answer holds about 48 KiB at most, its metadata line included: go on from next_offset, and from next_column when a line was too long for one answer; the parts read in turn are the whole content. An attachment comes as its metadata (type, size, SHA-256, width and height, how to link it, a download address valid for an hour or two), then the image itself for a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP of at most 3 MiB and 8000 pixels a side, or else a link to download it. Without the server's public address set (server.public_url) there is no download address: an image still comes itself, any other attachment as its metadata only, with a note saying so.

path.description: The path from the notebook's root: "A/B.md" for a page, "A/diagram.png" for an attachment.

column.description: The byte of the first line to start from, from 0: next_column of the previous answer. Default 0.

limit.description: At most this many lines, from 1. Default 2000.

account.name: search
account.title: Search the notebook's words
account.description: Full-text search of the notebook for words: the pages and attachments whose titles hold every term come first, then the pages whose contents do, each newest first, a page with an excerpt around its first hit. Terms are parted by spaces and match without case; Chinese text matches by pairs of characters, so a term of one Chinese character finds titles only. q is at most 256 bytes and 8 terms. The first page has count: exact, about or at_least. A page may hold fewer results than limit, even none, and still a next_cursor: a call checks a bounded number of contents; go on while next_cursor is set. building says pages queued in bulk (by a batch, an import, a background restore or revert, an upgrade) are not searched until the index catches up. For patterns, exact text and line numbers, use grep.

q.description: The words to find, parted by spaces: at most 256 bytes and 8 words.

limit.description: At most this many results, 1 to 50. Default 20.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

account.name: versions
account.title: List or read a page's versions
account.description: Without revision, list a page's versions, newest first: each with its revision, size, times, and the changeset that wrote it (its kind, client and author); the answer also has the page's current version. Go on with next_cursor while it is set. With revision, read that version's content as read reads a page: two text blocks, a line of JSON metadata (path, kind, revision, current_version, offset, column, lines, total_lines, byte_size, next_offset, next_column), then its lines exactly as stored; go on from next_offset, and next_column. The version answered has its own revision, which may be above the one asked for: an edit session's saves share one version. Revisions are for reading: write and edit take the page's version, from read. A page in the trash has no path: its versions are read in the web.

path.description: The page's path from the notebook's root, as "A/B.md".

revision.description: The revision to read, from 1. Without it, the list of the page's versions.

offset.description: With revision: the first line, from 1. Default 1.

column.description: With revision: the byte of the first line to start from, from 0: next_column of the previous answer. Default 0.

limit.description: Without revision: at most this many versions, 1 to 100, default 50. With revision: at most this many lines, from 1, default 2000.

cursor.description: Without revision: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

account.name: write
account.title: Write a page
account.description: Write a page's whole content by its path from the notebook's root; the path ends with .md. Without base_version, it creates the page, and the parent pages it lacks, empty, in one change; a path that is a page already is refused. With base_version, the version read, list or write gave, it replaces the content of the page at the path: refused when the page changed since, or when the path names another page now; read it again. When the page holds that content already, nothing is written and changed is false, with an older base_version of that page too, and while the page is being edited. The content is stored byte for byte: at most 5 MiB of UTF-8, without NUL. A page being edited in the web editor, by you too, refuses the write, saying by whom; the lock cannot be taken over. The answer has the page's path, node_id and version, changed (false when nothing was written), the nodes it created, and the changeset's id and time.

path.description: The page's path from the notebook's root, as "A/B.md": its ancestors' titles, then its own title and ".md".

content.description: The page's whole content, as it will be stored: frontmatter, byte order mark and line breaks included.

base_version.description: The page's version, as read, list or write gave it, to replace its content. Without it, the page is created.

account.name: lint
account.title: Check the notebook's health
account.description: Check this notebook's health from a snapshot for this call. Omit rule for counts and previews of the applicable rules; limit and cursor require rule. Set rule to read its items, then continue with next_cursor; pages may move between calls. count_capped marks a lower bound, not the end of pagination. target_cut marks a shortened display target, not its full identity; use item_key. Page and source items include their full paths.

rule.description: An exact health check rule. Omit for counts and previews; limit and cursor require a rule.

limit.description: At most this many items, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to continue after its last item.

account.name: pending_sources
account.title: List undigested sources
account.description: List an LLM Wiki's undigested sources from a snapshot for this call. LLM Wiki only: a standard notebook is refused. This is the undigested_sources health check, with each source's path, kind, bytes and original created_at; empty source pages are omitted. Continue with next_cursor; pages may move between calls. Each item keeps its complete item_key and cursor.

limit.description: At most this many items, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to continue after its last item.
